content: [{"_type":"block","style":"normal","children":[{"_type":"span","text":"GitDash is a fork of EmDash that runs with no server and no database service. Your content, schema and settings are JSON files in a Git repository. A CI job builds them into a static site, and you edit in the browser with EmDash's own admin, which commits straight back to the repository.","_key":"k1","marks":[]}],"markDefs":[],"_key":"k2"},{"_type":"block","style":"normal","children":[{"_type":"span","text":"This site is a GitDash site. The posts under Demo blog are sample content, so open the studio and try editing them.","_key":"k3","marks":[]}],"markDefs":[],"_key":"k4"},{"_type":"block","style":"h2","children":[{"_type":"span","text":"Why a fork","_key":"k5","marks":[]}],"markDefs":[],"_key":"k6"},{"_type":"block","style":"normal","children":[{"_type":"span","text":"EmDash is built for servers: Cloudflare Workers or Node.js, with SQL at request time. That is the right design for most sites, but it rules out free static hosting, and it means open source projects, docs and personal blogs need infrastructure they would rather not run. GitDash keeps EmDash's content model, templates and admin, and changes where the data lives and when pages are rendered.","_key":"k7","marks":[]}],"markDefs":[],"_key":"k8"},{"_type":"block","style":"normal","children":[{"_type":"span","text":"The fork stays close to upstream on purpose. Sign in with a fine-grained token, or with GitHub or GitLab if you set that up.","_key":"k19","marks":[]}],"markDefs":[],"_key":"k20","listItem":"bullet","level":1},{"_type":"block","style":"normal","children":[{"_type":"span","text":"Saving: a pending-changes tray, then one atomic commit through the GitHub or GitLab API.","_key":"k21","marks":[]}],"markDefs":[],"_key":"k22","listItem":"bullet","level":1},{"_type":"block","style":"normal","children":[{"_type":"span","text":"Comments: giscus on GitHub, or GitLab-native comments.
